title: Server performance profile
description: Answers one question: given this hardware and this objective, how should the engine be run? A profile is a recommended DEPLOYMENT configuration. It deliberately carries no measurement provenance - no commit, no binary hash, no corpus hash, no seed, no timestamp, no host address - because those belong to a run manifest, which references a profile by id. That separation is what lets a recommended configuration survive new binaries and new benchmark campaigns. A profile is either COMPLETE (every section present) or an ALIAS (profile.alias_of set and no other section). The loader enforces that split, because a schema-level conditional is harder to read than the rule it encodes.

alias_of.description: When present, this profile is a pointer. Every other section must be absent: an alias that repeats values is a second copy that will drift.

primary.description: ttfa = time to first audio. realtime_factor = generation time divided by audio duration after the first chunk, per request; below 1 means the stream keeps ahead of playback.

concurrency_range.description: The client-concurrency band this configuration was qualified over. Outside it the profile makes no claim.

preferred_concurrency.description: Only set when a measurement supports it; otherwise "unspecified". A string is allowed for the case a single integer cannot express: one qualified point per checkpoint size, e.g. "0.6B C12; 1.7B C10 (per checkpoint size)". Whatever form it takes, the evidence belongs in preferred_concurrency_evidence.

preferred_concurrency_evidence.description: What measurement promoted preferred_concurrency: run shape, date, and the KPI numbers that earned it. A preferred point without this is a preference, not a result.

quality_changes_allowed.description: Whether this profile is permitted to alter the audio relative to the reference precision.

parity.description: Operational ISA-lane contract. This is not a qualification claim: it declares the requested and expected resolved leaves that a preflight must verify before a benchmark can run.

features.description: Expected status, or an allowed status set when a common-control profile spans ISAs with different compiled capabilities.

tunable_flags.description: ISA/host-specific knobs that are intentionally not pinned by this semantic lane; a campaign must still record their resolved values.

l3_mib.description: Usable last-level cache in MiB. null = not established: on a cloud slice lscpu reports the SOCKET L3, not the slice share, and a guessed number is worse than none.

isa_features_absent.description: ISA features this host does NOT have, when their absence is the point of the profile. A cross-ISA screen exists to measure what happens without VNNI or without a matrix unit, and that has to be readable from the file rather than inferred from the cpu_family.

smt_policy.description: Whether SMT was ON or OFF for the canonical measurements on this host, and how to reproduce that. SMT is part of the experiment, not of the host description: a result measured with SMT on is not comparable with one measured with it off, and with SMT on a contiguous LOGICAL cpu slice hands two prefork workers the hyperthread siblings of the same physical cores.

canonical_topology.description: The worker x thread layout this host is qualified at, and which layouts are NOT valid for it. A topology from another host may be run here only as a labelled subset, stating which CPUs are unused. This matters beyond bookkeeping: INT8 AMX dispatch depends on rows per thread, so changing the layout can change which kernel is selected.

batch_size.description: In-flight cap per worker. client_concurrency is NOT engine batch: with W workers a worker sees B>=2 only when C>=2W.

max_queue.description: Requests allowed to WAIT for a slot. A full queue is answered 503 at admission rather than held open.

queue_timeout_ms.description: How long a waiting request may sit before it is answered 503. 0 means no deadline on the wait itself.

max_request_seconds.description: Per-request generation cap, in seconds. It is also what DERIVES the input-length limit, so it is an availability knob and a validation knob at once. 0 disables the cap and lets one caller hold a slot for as long as the token ceiling allows.

max_text_chars.description: Input-length limit in characters, passed as --max-text-chars. 'unspecified' does NOT mean unlimited: the server then derives the limit from max_request_seconds and the batch prompt budget, floors it at 200, caps it at the compiled 8192, and reports the effective number in /v1/health. Fix a value here only when a deployment needs a limit tighter than the derived one.

first_chunk_ramp.description: Frames per decode call for the leading chunks, in order.

precision.description: Per component, because "int8" names completely different paths in the talker, the speech decoder and the code predictor.

value.description: null means deliberately NOT set; the compiled default applies.

selected_leaves.description: The kernel leaf each stage RESOLVED to on this host, as read from --dispatch-map. Recorded when the point of the profile is which leaves are reachable at all (a cross-ISA screen), so the file states it instead of leaving it to be inferred from the cpu_family.

server_env_serialization.description: How the environment is handed to a harness --server-env argument. Comma: a space-separated list silently folds every later variable into the previous VALUE.

benchmark_family.description: The arrival model, because a threshold from one does not transfer to another. DIAGNOSTIC_CLOSED_LOOP is the deliberately weakest form: a short closed-loop A/B run to answer one question, never a qualification - a profile carrying it must stay unqualified.

source_commit.description: Short git revision of the tree the qualifying run was built from. A qualification that cannot name its commit is a claim about no particular code.

binary_sha256.description: sha256 of the engine binary that produced the numbers, or its first 32 hex characters. The build tag alone does not pin the compiler or the SIMD level.

measured.description: Per-concurrency measurements behind the claim, unrounded. Percentiles are taken over requests, never as a ratio of percentiles.

ttfb_p50_ms.description: send -> status line and headers parsed by the client.

ttfb_p95_ms.description: send -> status line and headers parsed by the client.

stream_rtf_p95.description: STREAM_RTF over requests. A mean rate: below 1.0 is capacity, not a proof that a player never stalls.

total_rtf_p50.description: Whole-request RTF including admission and prefill. A diagnostic that explains a KPI, not a KPI.

total_rtf_p95.description: Whole-request RTF including admission and prefill.

safe_start_p50_ms.description: safe_play_start: the earliest time after the request at which playback can begin and still finish without an underrun. Computed per request, then percentiled - never as TTFA plus a prebuffer percentile.

safe_start_p95_ms.description: safe_play_start p95. Under 1 s is the hard line; at or above it the configuration is not acceptable however good the RTF looks.

prebuffer_p95_ms.description: required_prebuffer: the smallest delay after first audio at which a 1x player then never pauses.

max_gap_p95_s.description: The largest inter-chunk gap. This is the mechanism behind the stall rates: it is what forces the prebuffer.

stall100_pct.description: Share of requests with at least one stall under a 100 ms jitter buffer, re-buffering after an underrun. The tightest of the four and the first to break.

stall250_pct.description: Share of requests stalling under a 250 ms jitter buffer.

stall500_pct.description: Share of requests stalling under a 500 ms jitter buffer.

stall1000_pct.description: Share of requests stalling under a 1000 ms jitter buffer. Zero here proves very little on its own.

audio_s_per_wall_s.description: Audio seconds produced per wall second across all streams: the throughput unit comparable with published figures for other engines.

completed.description: Requests that finished in the measured window.

rejects.description: Requests refused at admission (503). Intentional fail-fast rejects are an outcome, not an error.

timeouts.description: Queue or server-side request timeouts. These fail a run.

interpretation.description: What the measured block means and what it does NOT license. Required in spirit whenever a screen is partial: it is where 'do not promote this' is written down next to the numbers that might tempt somebody to.

status_matrix.description: The four separable claims, each answered on its own: IMPLEMENTED, PARITY_VERIFIED, PERFORMANCE_VERIFIED, DEFAULT_PROMOTED. They are recorded apart because they are routinely conflated, and 'it runs' is the one most often mistaken for the other three.

oneOf.description: The qualification did not fix this value. Never invent one.
